key_insight: OmniReasoner teaches omnimodal LLMs to reason over long audio-video by first scanning a cheap global preview and then selectively zooming into the most relevant moments. This makes long-context understanding more accurate without paying the cost of high-fidelity processing everywhere.
problem_solved: Long audio-video reasoning is hard because the decisive evidence is sparse, spread across modalities, and expensive to preserve at full resolution across an entire stream.
method: Build a low-cost global preview of the full audio-video stream to identify candidate evidence.
Use a native zoom-in tool to inspect only the critical segments before answering.
Post-train the model with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning so it learns when and where to call the tool.
impact: This approach can improve accuracy and efficiency for long-form multimedia tasks, especially where important cues are rare and easy to miss. For practitioners, it offers a practical way to scale omnimodal reasoning without brute-force high-resolution processing.

paper_title: OmniReasoner: Thinking with Long Audio-Video via Native Tool Use
